title: A Road Down With a Given Sum

concept.title: Hand the rest of the target down the tree
body: Is there a road from the root down to a **leaf** whose values add up to a given number `target`? Instead of adding values on the way down and comparing at the end, **subtract** each value from the target: at a node with value `v`, the rest of the road must add up to `target - v`. At a leaf the road is complete, and it is a good road exactly when the remaining target equals the value of the leaf.

Passing the changed target as an **argument** is a common way to carry information down a tree; nothing has to be undone afterwards. The road must end at a **leaf**: a node with one child is not the end of a road. The values can be negative, so you cannot stop early when the remaining target becomes negative.

statement: Given a binary tree and a number `target`, decide whether there is a road from the root down to a leaf (a node without children) such that the sum of the values of the nodes on the road equals `target`.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of a tree is at most 800.
hints: At a leaf, compare the remaining target with the value of the leaf.
At other nodes, subtract the value and ask both children.
Do not accept a road that ends in a node with only one child.

        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1

        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":

            queue.append(node.left)

explanation: The target shrinks by the value of each node on the way down; at a leaf the road is good when the leaf value equals what is left.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def has_path_sum(root, target):
    if root is None:
        return False
    if root.left is None and root.right is None:
        return root.val == target
    rest = target - root.val
    return has_path_sum(root.left, rest) or has_path_sum(root.right, rest)

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()
target = int(input())

print("yes" if has_path_sum(build_tree(vals), target) else "no")
